active.title: Compare two saved TestPilot runs without rerunning generation
active.body:
## Why

Saved TestPilot reports retain useful results, selected source and generated tests, but reviewing a before/after pair currently requires opening separate reports and manually matching their evidence. Add one local comparison without another generation or test run.

## Behavior

```bash
python -m testpilot compare --before out/before/report.json --after out/after/report.json --out comparison.html
```

The new output must not already exist. Both bounded saved reports are admitted completely before a completed HTML file is published. The offline page shows recorded results, selected-source context, generated-file changes, diagnostics, each run's own coverage, usage and rounds. It works without JavaScript and offers exact original JSON downloads, including formatting and extra fields.

Missing measurements remain unavailable; incomplete pricing remains unpriced. Matching target labels do not establish repository, commit, environment or test equivalence, and the view calculates no cross-run improvement. Literal report markup remains escaped text. Inputs are native generation `LoopResult` report.json files; the distinct recheck.json schema is refused.

The existing raw-diff, generation, targets and recheck commands remain intact. The only edits to the current CLI are the new parser and an early compare branch; the README receives one section. The final candidate is composed over `63174afd8e63a0ea562cf188b7d971522f017a30`. All **23 contribution blobs** and **1,020 unrelated base files** were verified before publication.

## Verification

- Original frozen source: **38 focused methods** and **36 inherited methods plus six subtests** pass. Four author browser groups exercise the portable page and exact downloads. The first phone grid overflow and its correction remain recorded.
- Independent root receiving generated **six real TestPilot/ScriptedModel/pytest/coverage reports** in separate percentage/ratio fixtures, then passed six actual compare commands and seven negative CLI processes. FIFO, invalid JSON, nonfinite values, Boolean counts, prior output and input aliases were refused while preserving bytes.
- **Six independent browser groups and six actual downloads** pass at desktop and 390 pixels. They verify real bug/fix counts, additional tests, missing coverage, no final result, distinct targets, native keyboard use and literal markup. Equal JSON values with distinct BOM/CRLF/Unicode bytes retain their separate exact identities. Zero external requests, page errors or console errors.
- Separate current-main receiving preserves the merged raw-diff/recheck work. The author ran five focused tests and six real coexistence command processes, including a model-free recheck and refusal of its different report shape. The root copied all 35 final source files, verified all 28 inherited source blobs against the authoritative tree, and reproduced the exact original comparison through the final CLI. The parser and renderer bytes are unchanged from independent browser receiving.

[Independent receiving](docs/receiving/saved-run-comparison-490fcd7c4056/INDEPENDENT_RECEIVING.md) and [source/archive identities](docs/receiving/saved-run-comparison-490fcd7c4056/source-publication.json) preserve scripts, real input reports, outputs, screenshots, downloads, raw receipts, the author archive and the independent archive. Precommit transport mistakes were rejected by exact blob checks and corrected before any branch publication; they did not change or rerun product source.

Hosted CI and actual merge-tree preservation will be recorded at normal integration.

Closes #26.

active.title: Preserve saved review artifacts when output staging fails
active.body:
## Scoped source contribution — estate-afe225d6c6be

A developer rerunning TestPilot into an existing `--out` directory can lose the last complete saved review if preparing or staging its replacement fails. The actual unmodified `write_outputs` truncates and writes the final patch, JSON, Markdown and HTML paths sequentially.

At native baseline `e1d87442eeecc8cf1b44ee3547849d5c1d030876`, a real 4096-byte file-size limit in an owned child reproduced two failures: an early patch write replaced the prior 237-byte patch with a truncated 4096-byte file; a later HTML failure had already replaced the earlier artifacts and truncated the previous complete HTML. An unrestricted changed-input control succeeded. Baseline receipt SHA-256: `cfd2d53bcff0d1a2654d3f4314aec994accf5b332a84393c6f47925ae7dedeaa`.

Fresh discovery main is `e2285d68b2ea5eb2158c0a7e0d936ce5d56f8ff5`. Its exact writer and incoming generation/diff changes will be received before edits; the original baseline keeps its actual source identity.

### Bounded behavior and source fence

Prepare all four output contents and stage complete files in the output filesystem before replacing a final artifact. A preparation, final-path admission or staging failure must preserve every existing final artifact and propagate the error. Reject observed non-regular or symbolic-link final targets before publication. Successful artifact bytes, names and returned path mapping remain compatible.

Final replacements occur only after staging succeeds. This scope does not promise an atomic four-file transaction, cross-process writer exclusion or power-loss recovery; a later replacement error must propagate honestly, with complete individually replaced files and the remaining publication limit documented.

Own only `testpilot/loop.py::write_outputs`, an optional new private output helper, focused tests, narrow output documentation and unique `docs/receiving/output-staging-afe225d6c6be/` evidence. Preserve current generation/fence/patch logic, HTML rendering, raw-diff transport, saved-test recheck, saved-run comparison #26, CLI dispatch, selector/model/sandbox/collector and their owners.

Engine execution authors the bounded implementation. Root owns all serialized GitHub writes and independent receiving/integration. Qualify with real isolated filesystem failures, changed-input success/byte controls, preparation/admission failures, cleanup and explicit late-replacement limits, current native suite and hosted checks. No model/provider call, real developer output directory or installed runtime is used.

completed_timeout.title: Return timed-out test runs when helpers keep output open
completed_timeout.body:
A timed-out pytest run can keep TestPilot's repair loop waiting indefinitely. The current handler kills the process group, then calls `communicate()` without a deadline; a detached helper can retain the stdout pipe. Captured text ending midway through a UTF-8 character can also raise `UnicodeDecodeError` instead of returning the timeout result.

Give POSIX post-kill output collection a **one-second drain budget**. If the pipe stays open, return the already captured diagnostics, preserve newline handling, close the reader and poll the killed leader. Invalid/incomplete captured text is represented with replacement characters. The sole runtime change is `testpilot/sandbox.py::_run`.

## Verification

- Exact initially published combined source on main `bc095b47f65805079ee4e9ef97971347fcdfbaa5`: native Python **3.12.14**, pytest **9.1.1**, coverage **7.16.2**, complete suite **91/91 passed, zero skips**.
- Six new real-process controls: **2 pass / 4 fail** on the original; **6 pass** on the candidate. The four initially failing controls are unchanged from before runtime editing: waiting/exited parent with a detached helper, a truncated multibyte diagnostic, and actual default `run_pytest` timeout followed by a fresh successful run. Normal combined output/status and empty timeout output remain covered.
- Independent root source review accepted runtime SHA-256 `f37cffae5cd8b8b527bd41ac6a9eb6dba0715e0bc6cb95684ac7964339eb10b3`. Its separately authored helper kept writing continuously: timeout 0.4 seconds returned in **1.402183 seconds**, retaining the parent diagnostic and **135 contiguous, nonduplicated lines**. The helper remained alive until the receiver's explicit cleanup.
- Actual authored generate/timeout/repair workflow: first timed-out pytest round **2.004 seconds**, versus the original **6.182 seconds**; then one generated test, two passing tests, three ScriptedModel calls and a patch accepted by `git apply --check`. Input files stay unchanged. No live model/provider was used.
- Before publication, the newly merged source-containment/CLI contribution was materialized exactly and the combined suite rerun. Tree `58ff128cbe53c2e8856563e44b1589e270e0ce91` was read back: all **11 payload files** match, all **91 unrelated current-main leaves** are preserved, **102 total leaves**, no unexpected entries.

The [receiving packet](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/testpilot/blob/f83d5614491f12ddeae5e917166f749f7a3cf7d0/docs/receipts/sandbox-deadline-bd1abdb2f886-20261008/README.md) includes baseline failures, the final suite output, workflow replay/results, the unchanged independent witness/output, and hash-bound source/evidence identities.

## Scope and receiving

A drain deadline is not an unconditional wall-clock guarantee for process creation, OS scheduling, repository copying or coverage setup. Escaped helpers are not contained; the receivers clean up only their own helpers. **The existing Windows reader-thread drain behavior is retained**; detached-process controls explicitly require POSIX and Windows execution is not claimed.

Existing loop/test preservation, source-containment/CLI, model and separate CI PR #1 scopes are unchanged. No installed-estate service was activated. Coordination: [issue #2 comment6055917934](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/testpilot/issues/2#issuecomment-6055917934). Contributor `chatgpt-astra-bd1abdb2f886-20261008 / estate_source`; source integration is delegated by the independent root reviewer.

## Final receiving after concurrent preservation integration

The existing loop/test-preservation contribution merged main `ca2e6c72743c5d3866f3f14189f1d4c3405f60bf` during receiving. Its 40 changed/new files were materialized exactly; the composed source passes **109/109 tests, zero skips**, and the real authored timeout/repair workflow passes on the current loop. [Complete final receiving log and workflow summary](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/testpilot/pull/5#issuecomment-6056736685). The independently reviewed runtime and PR head `f83d5614491f12ddeae5e917166f749f7a3cf7d0` remain unchanged.

completed_recheck.title: Add saved-test recheck without model calls
completed_recheck.body:
## Recheck the saved tests after a fix

A generation report already retains the exact proposed test files. This adds a usable `testpilot recheck` command that runs those bytes against a current checkout through the existing sandbox and generated-case collector, without invoking a model or replacing the original generation evidence.

```sh
python -m testpilot recheck \
  --repo /path/to/current-checkout \
  --report /path/to/original/report.json \
  --out /path/to/new-recheck-result
```

The result directory receives `recheck.json` and `recheck.md`. A previous recheck JSON can be reused. Exit status is 0 for current success, 1 for current failures or no retained passing cases, and 2 for admission/setup/output errors. `--python` preserves a selected project venv; `--timeout` uses the existing runner limit.

## Changes and ownership

- Add strict bounded saved-report admission, exact UTF-8 test-byte custody, and separate current results.
- Add an early CLI dispatch that returns before model construction.
- Add an opt-in `exact_files` sandbox mode for retained files. It creates missing tests with binary exclusive writes, accepts exact matching regular files without rewriting them, and preserves default generation behavior. This narrow scope extension follows a reproduced read-only 0444 failure; initial evidence is retained.
- Add 33 focused regression cases and the command guide in [docs/RECHECK.md](docs/RECHECK.md).

Ownership was recorded in [TestPilot #2](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/testpilot/issues/2#issuecomment-6060231013) and [HAMON #140](https://github.com/Jacob-Met/hamon/issues/140#issuecomment-6060236570). The exact accepted collector, model-timeout, HTML output and generation fence/patch contributions are preserved.

## Qualification and source custody

Ten real retained-report controls passed, including maintained buggy → fixed checkouts, exact applied read-only tests, conflicts, current existing-suite failures, timeout and selected project Python. |
| R2 on `e1d8744` | Only the new Python fixture changed to the project's existing `.pth` tooling-reuse pattern. The affected case passed. Three real-report controls preserved their outcomes against the exact accepted collector/HTML source. |
| Independent R2 review | Full source/CLI/sandbox/guide/test review accepted. Two actual CLI calls showed that forged historical “passed” metadata still gives current buggy exit 1 (three failures/one pass) and fixed exit 0 (four passes), with exact source, report and checkout preservation and zero model calls. |

Static receiving verifies those generation-only definitions and the unchanged recheck import/dispatch boundary. No later full native rerun is claimed. |
| R4 on `e2285d68` | Preserve accepted PR27 raw diff input. The three recheck additions inverse-remove to the exact incoming CLI; the other four owned product blobs stay unchanged. Eight affected tests and twelve subtests pass, followed by an actual buggy/fixed retained-report pair with zero recheck model calls and exact source/report preservation. |

Native qualification used ordinary-user Linux Python 3.14.4 and pytest 9.0.2, with no dependency installation or live provider calls. Initial failures, bounded capacity stops and later corrections remain separately identified.
